title: Material Conditional
body:
The **material conditional** `P→Q` is false in exactly one case, where the antecedent `P` is
true and the consequent `Q` is false. Every other combination makes it true.

```
 P  Q | P→Q
 T  T |  T
 T  F |  F     the only false case: the promise was broken
 F  T |  T
 F  F |  T     vacuously true: no promise was made
```

The bottom two rows are the ones that feel wrong. "If the moon is cheese then I am the king" is
true in this system, because the antecedent is false. The definition is chosen this way to keep
the connective truth-functional: the value has to be decided by the two parts alone, and the
only assignment that preserves the one thing a conditional clearly says, that you cannot have
the antecedent without the consequent, is the table above.

The cost is that material implication carries no notion of relevance or causation. "If Paris is
in France then 2+2=4" is true, and nothing about the first clause bears on the second.

Direction matters and reversing it is the standard error. `P→Q` and `Q→P` are different claims,
the second being the converse, and `¬Q→¬P` is the contrapositive and is equivalent to the
original. [[Modus Tollens]] is that equivalence used as a rule.
